samples.summary: harness-engineering.md still documents the removed warn-and-skip behaviour of `spec-to-pr.mjs review`
samples.evidence: Lines 2403-2406 read: "**Local review is a convenience, not authority:** `spec-to-pr.mjs review` runs the same lenses over the working diff, but needs `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` and degrades to a warn-and-skip when it is absent. The authoritative panel is still the cloud one". This change deletes exactly that skip (`ambientAuthNotice` + proceeding on the logged-in session) and the whole premise of the feature — recorded in docs/design/agentic-dev-loop.md §1.1 and CONTRIBUTING.md — is that for an ordinary branch the local run is the ONLY machine review, i.e. not a convenience pre-filter. The change updated agentic-dev-loop.md but left the second design doc describing the same command contradicting it. Nothing mechanical catches this (the docs lane only resolves backticked paths).

samples.summary: The carry-forward projection is mirrored rather than shared: the workflow's inline copy is left in place, guarded only by two substring assertions
samples.evidence: `carryForwardFindings` re-states the selection half of the projection in `.github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml:1007-1028`, and `prior-findings.test.mjs` guards it with `workflow.includes("norm(f.severity) === 'critical' ...")` / `workflow.includes("f.lane !== 'backlog'")`. The stated reason the copy cannot import is that the step's module graph lacks this file, but the same workflow already executes `.trusted/scripts/agent/prior-findings.mjs` as a node script at line 674, so the module is on disk in the workspace and the github-script step could call it. The two copies already differ beyond the declared 'transport' split: the cloud writes `severity: norm(f.severity)` (normalised) while the local one carries the raw value (asserted by the 'unknown severity is blocking' test carrying `"spicy"` through), and the local one adds `line`. A substring guard cannot see that class of drift, so cloud and local can carry differently-shaped prior findings for the same verdict.

samples.summary: Design doc says the carry-forward is "shared with the cloud's projection" when it is a hand-mirrored second copy
samples.evidence: §1.1 states the local loop "carries each round's still-gating findings into the next (`carryForwardFindings`, shared with the cloud's projection)". The cloud path does not call `carryForwardFindings`; `agent-review-panel.yml:1007-1028` keeps its own inline github-script implementation, and the new module's own docblock says the two "must agree by inspection". A design doc asserting shared code where there are two copies is the kind of cross-module prose claim this branch's own lessons file flags as uncovered.

samples.summary: The task doc's verification and known-limitations sections describe behaviour the final change does not have
samples.evidence: Line 85-86 records as verified: "`--round 4` prints the bound advisory and still runs". The shipped behaviour is the opposite — `roundBoundNotice` + `cmdReview` REFUSE past `MAX_SELF_REVIEW_ROUNDS` unless `--force`, which is what CLAUDE.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and `.claude/commands/self-review.md` document. Line 186 likewise still lists "A detached HEAD shares one round directory (the branch name is `HEAD`)" as a known limitation, which `branchKey` in this same diff fixes (and tests). The task record is the artifact a reviewer/archiver reads for what landed, so both entries misreport this change.

samples.summary: `printable`'s docblock cites `neutral()` in rebuttal.mjs as the same reasoning, but that helper solves a different problem
samples.evidence: `rebuttal.mjs:84` is `const neutral = (s) => str(s).replace(/<!--/g, "<!-‌-")` — HTML-comment-marker neutralisation for GitHub comment bodies, not C0/C1 control stripping for a terminal. The shared idea (model text is data) holds, but the citation invites a reader to expect an existing sanitiser they could have reused; there is none, which is worth saying plainly instead.
